newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

New Home Office proposals revealed in a Green Paper today outline plans for curfews to control children as young as five. In a bid to win the law and order vote over Labour Michael Howard announced he would scrap the 'age of innocence' rule which now allows tearaways between 10 and 13 to claim they do not know right from wrong.
LITTLEWOODS PUTS FOR SALE SIGN OVER STORES

Pools to stores group Littlewoods is selling up 135 of its High Street stores in a bid to raise 500 million stg. It is understood to want to concentrate on the home shopping market which is an area of fast growth.
COM CAB DRIVES TO AIM IN FACE OF PROTEST

Computer Cab, the London taxi operator has just published its prospectus to join the Alternative Investment Market. Just hours beforehand rebel cabbies went to court over the flotation. The company is seeking seven million stg from the stock market placing, mainly to pay for the Mobistar satellite tracking system.
FRANCE BIDS TO EASE THE FAILURES BURDEN

French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis is set to overhaul state- controlled companies at whose hands the French taxpayer has had to suffer financial mismanagement for the past decade. He promises to crackdown on those who have squandered public money whilst running state controlled companies and tighten the flow of civil servants between private and state owned companies.
